practice.foundation[4]: Standalone classification of a dot plot is not explicitly asked in the supplied booklet; matching in question 2 does not establish its intermediate classification as a separate type. Replace with an adapted Foundation box-plot classification item and update structure.

practice.development[0]: Replace the unsupported misconception-explanation task with an adapted box-plot shape question and update structure. Remove the false claim that the displayed median is close to the left edge, and correct the solution's assertion that median position never contributes to assessing skew.

practice.development[1]: Resolve the numerical inconsistency between the histogram and box plot $A$ before claiming they can represent the same dataset. Render the histogram with adjoining bins and explicit bin boundaries, and make the solution check compatibility rather than treating matching skew as sufficient.

practice.development[2]: Replace this standalone histogram-classification task with an adapted box-plot classification or display-matching question and update structure. The supplied booklet asks histogram matching, not standalone classification; the current continuous-time histogram also has gaps between bins.

practice.development[3]: Replace standalone dot-plot classification with an adapted box-plot classification or display-matching question and update structure; this classification is only an intermediate step in the booklet's matching question.

practice.development[5]: Correct the proposed matching box plot and its solution so its five-number summary agrees with the dot plot. Matching positive-skew direction does not make the current $A$ the same dataset.

practice.mastery[0]: Replace histogram-column prediction with an adapted Mastery box-plot classification or source display-matching task and update structure. The booklet does not ask this prediction type, and the solution claims histogram detail that a five-number summary cannot determine.

practice.mastery[1]: Replace the unsupported misconception-explanation task with an adapted Mastery box-plot classification item and update structure. Correct the solution's blanket claim that box-half widths are irrelevant to skew.

practice.mastery[2]: Replace the unsupported misconception task with an adapted Mastery box-plot classification item and update structure. Repair the answer and method: equal whiskers alone cannot override a substantially off-centre median or prove symmetry.
quiz.q2: Keep the classification and values, but repair option $3$'s explanation: whisker lengths provide evidence of skew, rather than being all that is needed to determine it in every box plot.

quiz.q3: Replace standalone histogram classification with an adapted booklet box-plot classification or display-matching question and update structure. The histogram also needs adjoining continuous-time bins; a modal bin centred at $35$ does not establish an exact raw-data mode of $35$, as option $3$'s explanation claims.

quiz.q4: Replace standalone dot-plot classification with an adapted booklet box-plot classification or display-matching question and update structure; the booklet does not explicitly ask this standalone type.

quiz.q5: Repair the plot or answer set to yield one defensible classification, and correct the solution's equal-whiskers-imply-symmetry rule. Give the positive- and negative-skew distractors distinct, specific explanations instead of the same single-median-line explanation.

quiz.q6: Make the histogram's bin boundaries explicit and adjoining, and correct the matching box plot to be numerically compatible. Recheck all four options and explanations so exactly one is correct; matching skew alone does not establish the same distribution.

quiz.q7: Repair the conflicting box-plot features or answer set to provide a defensible unique classification. Correct the solution and options $1$ and $3$ so they do not teach that only whisker lengths matter.

quiz.q8: Replace the unsupported dot-plot misconception-explanation task with an adapted booklet classification or display-matching question and update structure. Option $1$'s explanation must identify the actual error here: claiming a left-heavy concentration when the frequencies are symmetric.

theory: Present longer whiskers as evidence suggesting tail direction, not a universal determination of skew. Remove the claims that box-half widths and median position never matter: the booklet's Mastery question 9 has equal whiskers but a strongly off-centre median and is positively skewed, and lines 1841-1842 explicitly use median position alongside whiskers. Explain that approximate symmetry requires a centred median as well as balanced whiskers, and that a box plot cannot guarantee the detailed histogram shape or successive column heights.
summary: Replaced unsupported classification, prediction and misconception tasks with cited booklet box-plot classification types, corrected incompatible display matches and histogram bins, and repaired ambiguous quiz plots and explanations. Updated theory and affected solutions to consider median position alongside whiskers, explain the limits of box plots, and require numerical compatibility when matching displays; no whole items were removed.
reviewSummary: All 15 practice items and eight quiz questions have correct answers and use booklet question types, with exactly one correct option per quiz question and valid distractor explanations. The theory is consistent with the supplied teaching and figures; no worked examples or removals were supplied.
